sources.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide

rules.description: Target apogee for the scored 10K single-stage categories.

conditions: COTS is limited to solid or hybrid propulsion.
SRAD may use solid, hybrid, or liquid propulsion.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: 10,000 ft AGL apogee with commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) solid or hybrid rocket propulsion system

rules.description: Target apogee for the scored 30K single-stage and two-stage categories.

conditions: Single-stage COTS is limited to solid or hybrid propulsion.
Single-stage SRAD may use solid, hybrid, or liquid propulsion.
The two-stage 30K category permits any propulsion type.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: 30,000 ft AGL apogee Two Stage any propulsion type

rules.description: Target apogee for the scored 45K two-stage category.

conditions: The source defines no single-stage 45K category and permits any propulsion type for two-stage.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: 45,000 ft AGL apogee Two Stage any propulsion type

rules.description: Minimum payload mass carried by the launch vehicle.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: The launch vehicle shall carry no less than 4.4 lbs. of payload.

rules.description: Official-scale shortfall accepted without penalty; this is an inspection allowance, not a design minimum.

conditions: Applies only to the official competition weigh-in discrepancy.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: competition officials will accept payload weigh-ins as much as 5% (~0.2 lb.) less than the specified minimum without penalty

rules.description: Apogee-error window within which altitude-accuracy points are awarded.

conditions: Applies to the eight scored categories, not non-competing demonstrations.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: Points will be awarded for apogees within ±30% of the 10,000 ft AGL, or, 30,000 ft AGL, or 45,000 ft AGL target apogee

rules.description: Total zipper length above this threshold is classified as excessive recovery damage.

conditions: Postflight recovery-scoring criterion.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: Zippers with a total length greater than one (1) caliber ... are considered excessive damage.

rules.description: Discretionary maximum replacement time for damaged fins or boat tails designed for rapid replacement during recovery scoring.

conditions: Applies only to damaged fins or boat tails specifically designed for easy, rapid replacement.
Replacement components must be on hand and allowance remains at competition officials' discretion.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Rules & Requirements Document
citation.quote: replacement of damaged fins or boat tails specifically designed for easy, rapid replacement is allowed if such components are on hand and can reasonably be replaced within 30 minutes

rules.description: Minimum rail departure velocity evaluated at the effective rail length.

conditions: For tower launchers, evaluate when the center of pressure clears the tower (DTEG 5.3.3).
Cluster rockets must satisfy the minimum on any single motor in the cluster (DTEG 5.3.4).

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Teams shall design their rockets to attain a rail departure velocity of at least 25 m/s (82 ft/s) based on the effective length of the rail.

rules.description: Current actual launch-rail length published for single-stage rockets; effective rail length remains vehicle-dependent.

conditions: Published equipment value, not the effective rail length used to evaluate departure velocity.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Actual rail lengths are currently 17 feet for single-stage rockets and 21 feet for two-stage rockets.

rules.description: Current actual launch-rail length published for two-stage rockets; effective rail length remains vehicle-dependent.

conditions: Published equipment value, not the effective rail length used to evaluate departure velocity.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Actual rail lengths are currently 17 feet for single-stage rockets and 21 feet for two-stage rockets.

rules.description: An air-start motor must remain inhibited until the rocket reaches the specified fraction of simulated desired-firing altitude.

conditions: Applies to air-start motors and is one of several conditions that must all be met.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The rocket has reached an altitude of at least 70% of the simulated altitude at the time when initiator firing is desired

rules.description: Launch angle prescribed for the simulation used to set the air-start altitude threshold.

conditions: Applies only to the air-start threshold simulation, which must also use no wind.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: the simulation shall be performed at a 0° launch angle with no wind

rules.description: Maximum sustainer flight-angle deviation from vertical for air-start ignition.

conditions: Applies to ignition of air-start motors.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The sustainer flight angle is within 20° of vertical.

rules.description: Independently recovered bodies anticipated to exceed this apogee require dual-event recovery.

conditions: Applies per independently recovered launch-vehicle body, including payloads; two-stage boosters are included.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Each independently recovered launch vehicle body, including payloads, anticipated to reach an apogee above 457 m (1,500 ft) above ground level (AGL) shall follow a dual-event recovery operations concept. Boosters from two-stage rockets are subject to the dual-event provisions of this section.

rules.description: Independently recovered bodies released below this altitude are exempt from dual deployment.

conditions: The source does not resolve the exact 457 m boundary between its above/below wordings.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Independently recovered bodies (payloads) released at an altitude below 1,500 ft (457 m) AGL, are exempted from dual deployment

rules.description: Maximum AGL altitude for the main recovery deployment event.

conditions: Applies to any recovery method requiring a main deployment event.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The main deployment event for any recovery method shall occur at an altitude no higher than 457 m (1,500 ft) AGL.

rules.description: Launch-site elevation prescribed for drogue and landing descent-rate calculations.

conditions: Applies specifically to descent-rate calculations, not every trajectory calculation.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.section_title: Initial Deployment Event; Main Deployment Event
citation.quote: Descent rate calculations shall be based on a launch site elevation of 890 m (2,920 ft) MSL.

rules.description: Required drogue descent-rate band at the point of main deployment.

conditions: The source says between 20-40 m/s but does not explicitly define endpoint inclusion.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The descent rate under drogue shall be between 20-40 m/s (65-131 ft/s) at the point where the main parachute is deployed.

rules.description: Maximum vehicle descent rate at landing.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The vehicle's descent rate at landing shall be less than 11 m/s (36 ft/s).

rules.description: Maximum touchdown descent velocity for a payload recovered independently from the launch vehicle.

conditions: Applies only to deployable payloads that separate before landing.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Incorporate an independent recovery system, reducing the payload's descent velocity to less than 11 m/s (36 ft/s) at touchdown.

rules.description: Maximum number of independently recoverable bodies for a rocket with deployed payloads.

conditions: Applies to rockets with payloads deployed before landing.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Rockets with deployed payloads shall contain no more than a single (1) independently recoverable body.

rules.description: Attitude deviation from launch elevation that requires an active-control system to default neutral.

conditions: Applies only to launch vehicles implementing active flight controls.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Control actuator systems (CAS) shall default to a neutral state whenever ... the launch vehicle's attitude exceeds 30° from its launch elevation.

rules.description: 10K altitude condition that may end active-control boost-phase dormancy.

conditions: Applies only to active controls and is an OR alternative to boost end or passing max-Q, not an unconditional minimum activation altitude.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: For 10K flights: an altitude of 2,000 m (6,500 ft) AGL.

rules.description: 30K/45K altitude condition that may end active-control boost-phase dormancy.

conditions: Applies only to active controls and is an OR alternative to boost end or passing max-Q, not an unconditional minimum activation altitude.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: For 30K and 45K flights: an altitude of 6,000 m (19,600 ft) AGL.

rules.description: Minimum fin-flutter velocity margin above maximum expected rocket velocity.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Teams shall ensure that the fin flutter velocity of the rocket is at least 50% higher than the maximum expected rocket velocity.

rules.description: Typical single-stage launch elevation set by launch officials; not a hard design pass/fail limit.

conditions: Launch officials set the actual elevation and may require a different angle for safety.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Single-stage rockets are typically launched at an elevation angle of 84° ±2°

rules.description: Typical multi-stage launch elevation set by launch officials; not a hard design pass/fail limit.

conditions: Launch officials set the actual elevation and may require a different angle for safety.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: multi-stage flights are typically launched at 87° ±2°

rules.description: Minimum stability margin for subsonic flight from launch through first recovery deployment.

conditions: Subsonic regime; two-stage rockets evaluate the stack and sustainer separately.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: For subsonic flights, the minimum stability margin is 7.5% of the length of the rocket.

rules.description: Minimum stability margin for supersonic flight from launch through first recovery deployment.

conditions: Supersonic regime; two-stage rockets evaluate the stack and sustainer separately.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: For supersonic flights, the minimum stability margin is 10% of the length of the rocket.

rules.description: Maximum stability margin at launch.

conditions: Evaluated from the no-wind stability simulation required by DTEG 10.2.3.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The stability margin at launch shall not exceed 18% of the length of the rocket.

rules.description: Maximum stability margin through flight.

conditions: Evaluated from the no-wind stability simulation required by DTEG 10.2.3.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: The stability margin through the flight shall not exceed 25% of the length of the rocket.

rules.description: Minimum fin span stated by the DTEG, based on the largest-diameter tube in the rocket or stage.

conditions: For two-stage rockets, apply per stage; see README for the source's span versus semi-span terminology ambiguity.

citation.document_name: International Rocket Engineering Competition Design, Test, & Evaluation Guide
citation.quote: Teams shall not design rockets with a fin span less than 0.8 calibers, based on the largest diameter tube in the rocket
